ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in parallelogram $ABCD$, $E$ and $F$ are points on sides $AD$ and $BC$ respectively, and $\angle ABE = \angle CDF$. Quadrilateral $BEDF$ is a parallelogram; connect $CE$. If $CE$ bisects $\angle DCB$, $CF = 3$, and $DE = 5$, what is the perimeter of parallelogram $ABCD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Given that CE bisects $\angle BCD$, it follows that $\angle 1 = \angle 2$. Furthermore, since $AD \parallel BC$, it implies $\angle 1 = \angle 3$, which leads to $\angle 2 = \angle 3$, and consequently, $ED = DC = 5$. In quadrilateral $EBFD$, it can be deduced that $BF = ED = 5$. Hence, the perimeter of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ equals $2 \times (5 + 3) + 2 \times 5 = \boxed{26}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the external quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram, A, E, D are collinear on the upper side AD, and B, F, C are collinear on the lower side BC; internally, BE and DF are connected, forming quadrilateral BEDF; the line segment CE from C to E is also drawn. In the figure, E is on AD, F is on BC, and CE connects obliquely from the lower-right corner C to the point E on the upper side. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a parallelogram, AD ∥ BC, therefore ED ∥ CB. It is known that CE bisects ∠DCB, so ∠DCE = ∠ECB. Also because ED ∥ CB, ∠CED = ∠ECB. Thus ∠DCE = ∠CED, triangle CDE is an isosceles triangle, giving CD = DE = 5. Also because BEDF is a parallelogram, the opposite side BF = DE = 5. It is known that CF = 3, therefore BC = BF + FC = 5 + 3 = 8. The perimeter of parallelogram ABCD is 2(BC + CD) = 2(8 + 5) = 26.
